mechanism: Confirmed exactly as written, with the Core inventory corrected in one place. Core keeps ONE warnings map (refs/bitcoin/src/node/warnings.h:23-79, node/warnings.cpp) holding five ids at d3056bc: node::PRE_RELEASE_TEST_BUILD, inserted by the Warnings constructor when CLIENT_VERSION_IS_RELEASE is false (warnings.cpp:22-27); node::CLOCK_OUT_OF_SYNC, set by TimeOffsets::WarnIfOutOfSync when the median peer offset exceeds the threshold (node/timeoffsets.cpp:64); node::FATAL_INTERNAL_ERROR, set by AbortNode (node/abort.cpp:20); kernel::LARGE_WORK_INVALID_CHAIN, set by InvalidChainFound when a chain more than 6 blocks' worth of work longer than our tip is found invalid (validation.cpp:1950-1954); and kernel::UNKNOWN_NEW_RULES_ACTIVATED, set when CheckUnknownActivations reports an unknown version bit that reached activation (validation.cpp:2900-2906). All five reach the `warnings` field of getblockchaininfo (rpc/blockchain.cpp:1443), getnetworkinfo (rpc/net.cpp:734) and getmininginfo (rpc/mining.cpp:493) through GetWarningsForRpc. -alertnotify fires on only the TWO kernel ids, because AlertNotify is called from KernelNotifications::warningSet (node/kernel_notifications.cpp:30-47,79-83) and the three node:: ids are set directly on the map; the record's 'two warnings exist' is therefore right about the alerting path and understates the RPC field. Ours: -alertnotify appears exactly once in src/, as a name in define-core-only-options (src/config-options.lisp:435). An fbound sweep of every BITCOIN-LISP* package for a symbol containing ALERT returns NIL; a sweep for WARNING returns four unrelated symbols (two wallet per-call warning helpers, the settings-file warning key and its writer) and no registry. There is no best-invalid tracking (grep for best-invalid / InvalidChainFound: nothing), no CheckUnknownActivations analogue in src/validation/versionbits.lisp, no AbortNode and no time-offset warning -- getnetworkinfo even reports a hardcoded ("timeoffset" . 0) at src/rpc/net.lisp:341. The `warnings` field is the constant empty vector #() at src/rpc/blockchain.lisp:79, src/rpc/net.lisp:359 and src/rpc/mining.lisp:548.
consequence: Downgraded from S2 to S3, because the harm here is failure-to-notice rather than a wrong security posture: the node's chain selection, its RPC data and everything it does on the wire are unaffected, nothing irreversible happens, and the operator IS told at startup that -alertnotify has no effect (supplied-core-only-options returns ("alertnotify"), so the WARN at src/node/init.lisp:1664-1668 names it). What the warning line does NOT cover is the polling channel, and that half is a false negative rather than an absence: getblockchaininfo/getnetworkinfo/getmininginfo answer with a well-formed empty `warnings` array, which a monitoring pipeline reads as 'the node reports no problems' -- and the node has no capacity to report any. Executed, the node was driven into the state Core alerts on (a 10-block branch, well past Core's 6-block threshold, marked invalid so the invalid branch outweighs the tip) and all three arrays stayed empty. So an operator who has wired both of Core's channels -- the -alertnotify pager and the `warnings` poll -- gets silence from both while a probable consensus split or an unknown-rules activation is in progress. That is the top of S3 rather than S2: an operator watching for a chain split is blind, but the belief that is wrong is 'my node would tell me', not a belief about what the node is doing to their funds or their privacy.
evidence: Probe build/ga11v/p-alert.lisp (worktree fix/ga11v-options-s2a, warm image). (1) Config: args->start-node-plist on (-regtest "-alertnotify=/usr/bin/pager %s") => :PLIST (:LISTEN T :WALLET-NAMES NIL :NETWORK :REGTEST) -- the option reaches no keyword -- :SUPPLIED-CORE-ONLY ("alertnotify"), so it IS named in the startup WARN. (2) Exhaustive absence: :ALERT-FBOUND NIL; :WARNING-SYMBOLS only (("BITCOIN-LISP.WALLET" "%PUSH-WARNINGS") ("BITCOIN-LISP.WALLET" "%LOAD-ON-STARTUP-WARNING") ("BITCOIN-LISP.CONFIG" "SETTINGS-FILE-WARNING") ("BITCOIN-LISP.CONFIG" "+SETTINGS-WARNING-KEY+")) -- no AlertNotify, no registry. (3) END-TO-END: with-wallet-chain-node on regtest, generatetoaddress 10, then invalidateblock on the height-1 block => (:HEIGHT-BEFORE 10 :HEIGHT-AFTER-INVALIDATE 0 :INVALID-BRANCH-BLOCKS-AHEAD 10) -- the invalid branch outweighs the tip by 10 blocks, past Core's >6 threshold -- and both reads returned (:WARNINGS-BEFORE (:GETBLOCKCHAININFO #() :GETNETWORKINFO #() :GETMININGINFO #()) :WARNINGS-AFTER (:GETBLOCKCHAININFO #() :GETNETWORKINFO #() :GETMININGINFO #())). The reader is not vacuous: the assoc returned the pair holding #() rather than NIL, so the key exists and is genuinely empty. fix_shape: Build the registry first and the notifier second, in Core's shape: one small warnings module holding a map from warning id to message with Set/Unset semantics that report whether the state CHANGED (Core's insert-returned-inserted is what makes the alert fire once per transition rather than once per block), seeded with a pre-release-build entry, and one reader that renders the map as the array the three RPCs already have a slot for -- replacing the three literal #() at src/rpc/blockchain.lisp:79, src/rpc/net.lisp:359 and src/rpc/mining.lisp:548 with that reader is the whole RPC change. Then wire the producers: a best-invalid block-index entry maintained where blocks are marked invalid (src/validation/block.lisp %mark-block-subtree-invalid and invalidate-block), compared against the tip with Core's `> tip work + 6 * GetBlockProof(tip)` rule to set/unset LARGE_WORK_INVALID_CHAIN; a CheckUnknownActivations analogue in src/validation/versionbits.lisp called at tip update, gated on Core's MinBIP9WarningHeight, to set UNKNOWN_NEW_RULES_ACTIVATED. Only after the registry exists does -alertnotify become implementable: promote it out of define-core-only-options to a real string option and run the sanitized, single-quoted command with %s substituted on the KERNEL transitions only, in a detached thread, matching Core's AlertNotify -- the three node:: warnings must reach the RPC array without firing the pager. Ship it with a test that drives the invalid-branch state and asserts a non-empty array, keeping a clean-chain empty-array run as the positive control so the assertion cannot pass vacuously.
